title: The toolchain
summary: Organizes coding-assistance tools by task, interaction style, prompt construction and model or hosting choices. The framework helps separate what a tool does from how a developer supplies its context.
limitation: A July 2023 conceptual landscape, not a comparative benchmark or a current product inventory.
topics: K:Developer workflow and adoption; K:Agent context and persistent memory

title: Median - A tale in three functions
summary: Examines three generated median implementations and the defects or side effects that a knowledgeable developer must recognize. The example makes the choice of test expectations part of the engineering work.
limitation: One small TypeScript example; neither defect prevalence nor a general model-quality comparison was established.
topics: K:Independent verification and oracles; K:Automation bias and trust

title: In-line assistance - when is it more useful?
summary: Discusses when inline suggestions help, considering task familiarity, technology, change size, developer experience and the effort of checking or reworking the output.
limitation: Experience-based guidance, largely from experienced developers; usefulness is not a measured universal productivity effect.
topics: K:Developer workflow and adoption; K:Human cognitive load; K:Economic costs and return

title: In-line assistance - how can it get in the way?
summary: Describes assistants repeating poor patterns from their context and the burden of continually judging suggestions. Relates these experiences to automation bias, anchoring and reluctance to discard generated work.
limitation: Qualitative examples and interpretive mechanisms, not measured frequencies of bias or review fatigue.
streams: T:Verification & review; T:System knowledge & memory; T:Code quality & security
topics: K:Automation bias and trust; K:Human cognitive load; K:Agent context and persistent memory

title: Coding assistants do not replace pair programming
summary: Argues that code assistance does not replace the human knowledge sharing, collaboration and collective understanding associated with pair programming. Tools can instead be used by a human pair.
limitation: An argument about the functions of pairing; not a controlled comparison of pairing arrangements.
streams: T:Skills & learning; T:Engineering structure; T:System knowledge & memory
topics: K:Human-agent collaboration; K:Ownership and knowledge transfer; K:Skills formation and teaching

title: TDD with GitHub Copilot
summary: Explores assistance during red, green and refactor steps. Human test intent and assertions remain important; suggestions can help implementation while also overproducing code or struggling with refactoring.
limitation: Experience with a human-led workflow and an early tool generation; not evidence about fully autonomous TDD or a causal quality gain.
topics: K:Independent verification and oracles; K:Human-agent collaboration

title: How is GenAI different from other code generators?
summary: Contrasts generative assistance with model-driven development and domain-specific code generators. Examines how control and abstraction differ when generation draws on broad learned patterns rather than an explicitly designed transformation.
limitation: Conceptual comparison; it does not demonstrate the reliability or economic superiority of either approach.
topics: K:Specifications and governance; K:Architecture and modularity

title: How to tackle unreliability of coding assistants
summary: Frames confidence in assistance around feedback, the developer’s ability to check an answer and the consequences of error. Proposes timeboxing unproductive assistance and retaining responsibility for the result.
limitation: Personal heuristics rather than calibrated reliability estimates; informal numerical intuitions are not treated as measured rates.
streams: T:Verification & review; T:What agents can do
topics: K:Agent failure and escalation; K:Independent verification and oracles; K:Automation bias and trust

title: Onboarding to a 'legacy' codebase with the help of AI
summary: Recounts work on an unfamiliar Bahmni/OpenMRS issue. AI helped with terminology and code navigation, but environment setup, fixtures and mocking remained obstacles, and the issue was not solved in the attempt.
limitation: One exploratory onboarding attempt; no measured reduction in onboarding time or demonstrated long-term comprehension.
topics: K:Onboarding and developer fluency; K:System understanding and rationale

title: Building an AI agent application to migrate a tech stack
summary: Builds a tool-using agent to migrate tests from Enzyme to React Testing Library. The account exposes file-editing, test-feedback and context-management problems alongside successful transformations.
limitation: A bounded migration experiment with substantial failures; not proof of reliable autonomous migration across a codebase.
streams: T:What agents can do; T:Code quality & security; T:System knowledge & memory
topics: K:Agent failure and escalation; K:Long-running agent execution; K:Independent verification and oracles

title: Expanding the solution size with multi-file editing
summary: Examines how multi-file edits enlarge the unit of AI-assisted work. Larger suggestions create new checking demands, including unrelated changes, and motivate layered feedback and comprehensible module boundaries.
limitation: A tool-use snapshot and qualitative experience; no comparative defect rate or current feature guarantee.
streams: T:Code quality & security; T:Verification & review; T:What agents can do
topics: K:Architecture and modularity; K:Review capacity and maintainers; K:Developer workflow and adoption

title: What role does LLM reasoning play for software tasks?
summary: Questions where model reasoning adds value to coding tasks compared with supplying repository context and useful tool feedback. Considers debugging and planning as possible settings for investigation.
limitation: Tentative analysis from February 2025, not a current model-feature comparison or evidence that reasoning always helps or harms coding.
streams: T:What agents can do; T:System knowledge & memory
topics: K:Evaluation methodology and baselines; K:Agent context and persistent memory

title: The role of developer skills in agentic coding
summary: Uses agent missteps to explain why decomposition, debugging, design judgment and checking remain valuable. Separates immediate completion from team iteration and the lifetime of the codebase.
limitation: Experience-based examples, not a measured skills intervention or a forecast of developer employment.
streams: T:Skills & learning; T:Code quality & security; T:Engineering structure
topics: K:Skills formation and teaching; K:Technical debt and complexity; K:Human-agent collaboration

title: Guiding an LLM for Robust Java ByteBuffer Code
summary: Follows a developer–LLM dialogue about Java ByteBuffer header access. The engineer uncovers problems with mutable buffer position and guides the design toward clearer access and encapsulation.
limitation: An illustrative dialogue; removing position mutation does not by itself establish thread safety or general performance.
topics: K:Architecture and modularity; K:Independent verification and oracles; K:System understanding and rationale

title: Building TMT Mirror Visualization with LLM: A Step-by-Step Journey
summary: Describes building a telescope-mirror visualization with unfamiliar tools. Small geometric steps, visual checks and domain knowledge guide successive changes while the developer learns the implementation approach.
limitation: A personal prototype-building account; neither retained learning nor broader productivity was evaluated.
streams: T:Skills & learning; T:What agents can do
topics: K:Skills formation and teaching; K:Human-agent collaboration; K:Developer workflow and adoption

title: Coding Assistants Threaten the Software Supply Chain
summary: Analyzes the attack surface created when coding assistants consume project instructions and invoke tools with developer privileges. Discusses poisoned context, dependency risks and boundaries around execution.
limitation: Security analysis rather than an attack-incidence study. Protocol and tool details belong to the May 2025 publication context.
topics: K:Prompt injection and malicious tools; K:Dependencies and agent supply chain

title: Building Custom Tooling with LLMs
summary: Recounts extending PlantUML with custom visualization tooling. The developer uses generation and feedback to build the tool, while shaping abstractions and keeping the resulting code understandable and maintainable.
limitation: One custom-tooling case; lower perceived effort is not a controlled productivity estimate.
streams: T:Code quality & security; T:Productivity; T:System knowledge & memory
topics: K:Architecture and modularity; K:System understanding and rationale; K:Developer workflow and adoption

title: Autonomous coding agents: A Codex example
summary: Inspects a background agent making a small Haiven change. The execution trace reveals code-search behavior, missing executable checks and inconsistent reuse across attempts, distinguishing unattended execution from accepted work.
limitation: A small dated tool experiment; not a model ranking or a general estimate of autonomous success.
streams: T:What agents can do; T:Verification & review
topics: K:Agent failure and escalation; K:Code reuse and duplication; K:Independent verification and oracles

title: I still care about the code
summary: Argues that responsibility for operational software still requires understanding code and its risks. Contrasts probabilistic generation with designed language translation and relates oversight to possible error consequences.
limitation: A professional position, not a calibrated threshold for how much review every change requires.
topics: K:Automation bias and trust; K:System understanding and rationale; K:Ownership and knowledge transfer

title: Partner with the AI, throw away the code
summary: In a Go/MySQL performance investigation, generated helpers, experiments and unsuccessful rewrites helped the developer understand the problem before rewriting the core solution. Useful assistance can therefore leave little accepted generated code.
limitation: A single client case; code-acceptance rate is questioned, but a general AI-caused productivity gain is not measured.
topics: K:Output versus shipped value; K:Evaluation methodology and baselines; K:System understanding and rationale

title: To vibe or not to vibe
summary: Describes decisions about oversight using the chance of an error, its impact and the ability to detect it. The examples favor situation-dependent attention over a single rule for all generated code.
limitation: A qualitative risk heuristic and personal experience; not a statistically calibrated risk model.
topics: K:Automation bias and trust; K:Human-agent collaboration

title: Anchoring AI to a reference application
summary: Explores using a runnable reference application to guide changes across services. A scoped comparison and a reviewed change report precede implementation, raising a choice between AI-based propagation and deterministic transformations.
limitation: A small reference-update example; consistency and maintainability at organizational scale remain untested.
streams: T:System knowledge & memory; T:Code quality & security; T:Engineering structure
topics: K:Architecture and modularity; K:Agent context and persistent memory; K:Specifications and governance

title: Understanding Spec-Driven-Development: Kiro, spec-kit, and Tessl
summary: Distinguishes spec-first, spec-anchored and spec-as-source approaches through three tool explorations. Examines persistent specifications, task sizing, brownfield fit, instruction following and documentation overhead.
limitation: A dated exploratory comparison, not controlled evidence for SDD effectiveness. The author’s questions about specification overhead and source-of-truth claims are retained.
topics: K:Specifications and governance; K:Developer workflow and adoption; K:Agent context and persistent memory

title: Assessing internal quality while coding with an agent
summary: Uses a CCMenu feature change to inspect internal quality. A fix that compiles can still erode the intended type model, introduce duplication or add unnecessary mechanisms; expert examination exposes those differences.
limitation: The author presents an anecdote, not a study; observations do not establish a population-level quality effect.
topics: K:Technical debt and complexity; K:Code reuse and duplication; K:Architecture and modularity

title: Context Engineering for Coding Agents
summary: Organizes context features by who invokes them: a person, the model or agent software. Discusses rules, skills, subagents, external context and hooks as parts of the developer experience.
limitation: Feature and practice snapshot, not proof of effectiveness or enforcement. Adding more configuration can produce contradictions or an illusion of control.
topics: K:Agent context and persistent memory; K:Developer workflow and adoption; K:Specifications and governance

title: Harness Engineering - first thoughts
summary: Interprets a reported harness through context, architectural constraints and codebase maintenance. Raises questions about reusable harnesses, constrained topologies and the effort of retrofitting existing systems.
limitation: A reaction to another organization’s account, not an independent experiment. The author explicitly notes a gap in the reported functional verification.
topics: K:Architecture and modularity; K:Independent verification and oracles; K:Long-running agent execution

title: Humans and Agents in Software Engineering Loops
summary: Distinguishes the why loop that pursues outcomes from nested how loops that build software. Proposes human work on the loop: improving guidance, checks and workflow rather than only editing individual outputs.
limitation: A conceptual operating model. Its proposed agentic improvement flywheel is not a demonstrated organizational or reliability result.
topics: K:Human-agent collaboration; K:Long-running agent execution; K:Specifications and governance

title: Viability of local models for coding
summary: Frames local agentic coding as a combined hardware, model, runtime, context and tool-calling problem. The account separates being able to run a model from obtaining usable results.
limitation: A personal hardware/tool snapshot. Explanations for observed configuration differences are hypotheses; code quality was not systematically evaluated.
streams: T:What agents can do; T:Economics; T:System knowledge & memory
topics: K:Agent context and persistent memory; K:Economic costs and return; K:Evaluation methodology and baselines

title: Experiences with local models for coding
summary: Presents a viability funnel and compares manual trials, a small automated evaluation and everyday local-model use. Outcome sensitivity to task, context and configuration makes simple capability claims difficult.
limitation: Two principal JavaScript/TypeScript tasks and small uneven repeat counts; one-shot automated trials differ from interactive work and do not establish a general ranking.
streams: T:What agents can do; T:Productivity; T:System knowledge & memory
topics: K:Benchmarks and construct validity; K:Evaluation methodology and baselines; K:Agent context and persistent memory

title: The Economic Benefit of Refactoring
summary: Repeats one representative change as a large Rust data-access module is refactored. Estimated input-token use falls after decomposition permits more selective code reading, connecting architecture to inference work.
limitation: One application and change, approximate token counting and incomplete refactoring-cost accounting; this does not establish general ROI or savings for every future task.
topics: K:Economic costs and return; K:Architecture and modularity; K:Code reuse and duplication

title: TDD inside the agent loop - theater or actual value?
summary: Separates human-authored tests, a human review checkpoint and TDD entirely inside an agent loop. The small exploratory comparison found no clear advantage for fully internal TDD in model-judged quality or mutation scores.
limitation: Small greenfield tasks, imperfect adherence and an LLM-defined quality rubric. Reported aggregate tokens include cache rereads and are not equivalent to billed cost; no universal conclusion about human-led TDD follows.
topics: K:Independent verification and oracles; K:Evaluation methodology and baselines; K:Economic costs and return

title: An Accidental Blackboard
summary: In a simulated airline exercise, shared plans and frequent repository updates became an improvised coordination surface for agents. The account connects this behavior with the blackboard pattern and describes resulting CI pressure.
limitation: A practice exercise, not a deployed airline system. The author explicitly questions reproducibility; the coordination mechanism was emergent rather than experimentally isolated.
topics: K:Human-agent collaboration; K:Agent context and persistent memory; K:Long-running agent execution

title: Are Harnesses Worth the Cost?
summary: Compares development with and without a behavioral harness against a separate acceptance suite. On the selected service, the stronger model passed both conditions; a cost-optimized model passed more consistently with harness feedback, at greater per-attempt effort.
limitation: Ten paired runs per model on one unusually detailed greenfield Java brief. Guides and sensors changed together; estimated generation costs omit harness authoring, review and repairs. Final-gate-only use is proposed, not tested.
topics: K:Economic costs and return; K:Independent verification and oracles; K:Specifications and governance
